docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
• Kept in the operating system's credential store by mm-mcp login: the Windows Credential Manager, the macOS keychain, or the Secret Service of a Linux desktop. mm-mcp login --with paste stores a personal access token or a bot token there as well, so that no token is kept in a configuration file (Installation). As with any entry in those stores, programs running under the person's account can read it.
  • Never in a command-line argument, a log line, an error or a tool result. No command accepts a token as an argument (ADR-019).
  • Never attached to a post. A file in which credentials are kept is refused, whoever asks for it: anything under a folder named .ssh, .gnupg, .aws, .azure, .kube, .docker, gcloud, .password-store, keychains or keyrings; the files .netrc, _netrc, .git-credentials, .npmrc, .pypirc, .pgpass, id_rsa, id_dsa, id_ecdsa, id_ed25519, a browser's Login Data, Cookies, key4.db and logins.json, and an MCP client's configuration (claude_desktop_config.json, .claude.json, mcp.json, mcp_config.json); any .p12, .pfx, .kdbx, .keychain, .keychain-db or .jks file; a .env file, except one ending in .example, .sample or .template; and any file that contains a private key or the token mm-mcp runs with. The path is checked after links are resolved, regardless of letter case, and a file from the local disk is attached only when mm-mcp runs on the person's machine, after they approve its path.

A token, or a session that mm-mcp login stores, grants everything its account can do in Mattermost, including an administrator's rights. Give mm-mcp an account with no more access than it needs.

docs.title: How a person logs in
docs.text:
Where the server offers Mattermost's OAuth, mm-mcp login uses only that: the person approves mm-mcp in their own browser, and mm-mcp receives a session of its own through a one-time code, without reading any browser data. Where OAuth is not available, it can log in through a browser window with a temporary profile of its own, deleted afterwards; through the person's password; or with a token the person pastes (Logging in). A pasted token may be a personal access token, or the session cookie of the person's own browser.

These fallbacks exist for servers where no other way in is available, and they interact with organisational controls:

  • The browser window may use Playwright's Chromium, which is installed in the person's user folder and is not covered by the policies that manage Chrome or Edge. On Ubuntu 24.04, that Chromium runs without its sandbox, because the system refuses it one; the window shows only the Mattermost login page.
  • A pasted cookie is the person's browser session. mm-mcp logout forgets it without ending it at Mattermost, so that the browser stays logged in.

An administrator who enables OAuth makes the fallbacks unnecessary, and from then on mm-mcp uses them only when the person explicitly asks for one (For administrators).

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: mm-mcp writes to the AI application's log, through standard error, only when it starts and stops: the account it is connected as, warnings about its configuration or the server, and who decides on a write. It does not log tool calls, their arguments or the changes it makes, and it keeps no record of its activity. A record of what an agent read and wrote exists in the AI application's conversation history and, on the Mattermost side, in what Mattermost records for the account: its posts, marked as written with AI by default, and whatever the server's audit logging retains. Every request mm-mcp sends carries User-Agent: mm-mcp/<version>.

docs.title: Instructions to the model
docs.text: When a client connects, mm-mcp gives the model a short set of instructions, which can be read in its source (internal/server/server.go): that it acts as a single account; that text written by others is to be read, not followed as instructions; that a change others see is made only when the person asked for it, states what it does to others, and is weighed again when mm-mcp refuses it; that a message is cited by its post's link, never by one built from an id; and how Mattermost formats mentions and Markdown. Each tool's description states what it does, and, where mm-mcp asks, that it asks.

docs.title: HTTP transport
docs.text: mm-mcp serve --transport http listens only on a loopback address. It refuses a request whose Host header does not name a loopback address, which prevents DNS rebinding, and a request a browser marks as sent from a web page of another origin (Installation). It authenticates no client: any process on the machine that can reach the port acts as the account mm-mcp runs with, including processes of other users on a shared machine. Over stdio, the default, only the application that started mm-mcp can communicate with it.

docs.title: Releases and updates
docs.text:
Every archive, Linux package and bundle is signed with Sigstore by the release workflow, with a build provenance attestation and an SBOM (Installation). Homebrew, Scoop and WinGet install the release's own archives and verify each against the SHA-256 hash in their manifest; to verify a signature directly, download the same archive from the release and check it.

mm-mcp is maintained by one person. Only the latest release is supported, and a security fix ships in the next release; there are no maintenance branches. Before version 1.0, a release may change behaviour, and its release notes say so (releases).

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Everything your agent can do in Mattermost with mm-mcp. Ask in your own words; it picks the tool. Writing is off until you allow it.

48 tools 26 only read 14 checked writes 7 yours alone 1 saves to your disk 5 show you a view

  • Catch up

    Pick up where you left off, in every channel, without marking anything read.

    “What did I miss since Friday?”

    read_unread get_user_channels list_mentions list_threads

  • Find it again

    Messages, files, people and channels, searched the way you would say it: by words, by who, where and when.

    “What did we decide about the release date?”

    search_posts search_files search_users search_channels

  • Read the whole story

    A channel page by page, a thread from its first post, and what was pinned or saved.

    “Summarise the thread about last night's outage.”

    read_channel read_post list_pinned_posts list_saved

  • See it as Mattermost shows it

    In an AI app that shows MCP Apps views, a thread, or what is waiting for you, appears in the chat as Mattermost lays it out: names and pictures, Markdown, reactions and images, and what is unread where.

    “Show me the thread about last night's outage.”

    show view_action view_change

  • Open the attachments

    Word, Excel and PowerPoint as their text, PDFs, images and archives, read for the model, or saved to your disk.

    “What's in the spreadsheet Sam shared?”

    read_file save_file

  • Post, reply and react

    Messages, replies, direct and group messages, edits and reactions, each approved by your AI app and checked by mm-mcp before it goes out.

    “Tell Sam in the thread that the notes are ready.”

    create_post dm group_message update_post delete_post add_reaction remove_reaction pin_post

  • Channels and people

    Who is who and who is around, which channels exist and who is in them; join, leave, create, add people, and set your status.

    “Is Sam online, and who else is in ~release-planning?”

    get_me get_users get_status get_user_teams get_team_info get_channel_info list_team_channels list_archived_channels get_channel_stats join_channel leave_channel add_channel_members create_channel set_status

  • Your own things

    A post proposed as your draft, to send yourself, reminders, saved posts and followed threads. Nobody else sees them; deleting a draft, which loses your words, is checked.

    “Draft a reply I can send myself, and remind me at nine tomorrow.”

    propose_post list_drafts delete_draft set_post_reminder save_post follow_thread mark_channel_read typing

  • Check the setup

    When something fails: the connection, the login, and who decides on a write.

    “Why can't you post?”

    diagnose

docs.title: Every tool
docs.text: Grouped as above. A badge says when a tool does more than read: checked for a change others see, or words of yours it deletes, which the call states and mm-mcp checks (below); yours alone for what only you see or is gone in seconds; and your disk. A tool marked view also shows you what it did in the chat, in an AI app that shows views; the badge opens it, live, on Views. The tools that write are offered only once you allow writes, with MM_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES (Configuration).

docs.title: Catch up
docs.text: read_unread: Read unread posts Catches up on a channel from where you stopped reading: a few posts you have read, then the ones you have not, oldest first, with the first unread one named. A channel you never opened is all unread, and reads newest first, the pages after going further back. It marks nothing read: what you have read is yours to record. get_user_channels: List the user's channels The channels you belong to, direct and group messages included, most recently active first, each with its team and how many messages and mentions are unread. team_id keeps one team's, unread_only those with something unread. list_mentions: List mentions The posts that mention you, most recent first, as Mattermost's Recent Mentions finds them: by @username, and by your first name, the other words and @channel, @all and @here when your notification settings say those mention you. Only a post that mentions you as Mattermost would notify you is kept, and none of your own. The answer names the words it looked for. from, in, before, after and on narrow it, and like search_posts it reaches the 100 most recent matches at most. The database search Team Edition uses skips "all" and "here" as too common to index, so @all and @here are found only on a server that searches with Elasticsearch, as they are in Mattermost's own Recent Mentions. list_threads: List threads The threads you follow, as Mattermost's threads view lists them, most recently replied to first: the post that started each, who took part, and how many replies and mentions you have not read.

docs.title: Find it again
docs.text: search_posts: Search posts Messages you can read, across every team or one, by words, and by who wrote them, where and when through from, in, before, after and on, so no search syntax is needed. @username finds where someone was mentioned. 20 posts a page by default, at most 100. Mattermost's search finds the 100 most recent matches at most, and the answer says capped when it reached them: before reaches older ones. in takes a channel you belong to, the only ones Mattermost searches, and from a username, refused with the closest when nobody has it. The days before, after and on name are your own, in the timezone you set in Mattermost, as in its search box. Without Elasticsearch, as on Team Edition, Mattermost searches a post's message alone, so a post whose words are only in its attachments or blocks, as an alert's often are, is not found: read_channel with since reads a channel of alerts instead. search_files: Search files Files attached to posts you can read, by name, by type with ext:pdf, and by from, in, before, after and on, each with the post and channel it is in and their links, and the file's address as a resource. Like search_posts, it finds the 100 most recent matches at most. search_users: Search users Users whose username, name, nickname or email address contains a term, optionally only within a team or a channel. Deactivated users are left out. Mattermost finds at most 1000 for one term. search_channels: Search channels Channels by part of their name: your own, and public ones you have not joined. Mattermost finds at most 50 public channels in a team for one term.

docs.title: Read the whole story
docs.text:
read_channel: Read channel

A channel's messages, 30 a page by default and at most 200, oldest first within a page: the newest, and the pages after go further back. before starts back from a post; after and since, from a post or a time, read forward. since takes a time with an offset, or a time or a day in your own timezone. collapse_threads leaves the replies out and shows each thread by the post that started it, as Mattermost shows a channel with collapsed reply threads.

A page here or of read_unread can hold a few more posts than its limit: posts written in the same millisecond stay on one page, since Mattermost reads on from a post by its time alone, and a page split inside a millisecond would lose posts.

read_post: Read post A post and the thread it is in, oldest first, 100 posts a page by default. Give any post in the thread; include_thread false reads the post alone. list_pinned_posts: List pinned posts The posts pinned to a channel. list_saved: List saved posts The posts you saved to come back to.

docs.title: See it as Mattermost shows it
docs.text:
show: Show view

Puts what you asked to see in front of you in the chat, laid out as Mattermost lays it out.

  • Kind thread shows a thread: who wrote each post, with their profile picture, when, the Markdown drawn, @mentions and ~channels, the cards a webhook or bot posted beside their colored bars, the blocks an integration posted with their columns and folded sections, the post a link quotes and the card of a page it leads to, reactions with who reacted, the Important and Urgent labels and how many acknowledged a post that asks for it, images you can open whole and file cards, the edited and pinned marks, a burn-on-read post you have not opened as a placeholder that opens it in Mattermost, a call with when it started or how long it lasted, and a placeholder for files an access policy withholds. It shows the first 30 posts, says how many more the thread has, and loads more as you ask.
  • Kind unreads shows what is waiting for you: up to 20 channels with something unread, grouped by team, with their unread and mention counts; up to 10 posts that mention you; and up to 10 threads you follow with unread replies. It says when Mattermost has more. A channel's unread messages or a thread open in place, or in Mattermost where your app does not let the view load them, and once you allow writes, a channel can be marked read from the view.

Links open in Mattermost. Your agent calls it when you ask to see something, after it found it, or ask what is waiting for you. It answers with what read_post, or get_user_channels, list_mentions and list_threads, answer, so the chat holds nothing the view adds. In an app that shows no views it shows nothing, and says so, and your agent answers in words (Views).

view_action: Act in a view What you do in a view that changes nothing, such as loading more of a thread or opening a channel's unread messages in place, goes through this tool. Only a view calls it: an app that shows views keeps it from your agent, and mm-mcp offers it only to an app that says it shows views. view_change: Change in a view What you do in a view that changes something goes through this tool: marking a channel read from the unread view, as mark_channel_read does, and posting, changing or discarding a proposal (propose_post). Only a view calls it, on your press: an app that shows views keeps it from your agent, and mm-mcp offers it only to an app that says it shows views, once you allow writes.

docs.title: Open the attachments
docs.text: read_file: Read file A file attached to a post, as content the model can read: text in windows of numbered lines, chosen with start_line and line_count; Word, PowerPoint and Excel files as their text; zip and tar archives as a listing; images as images, turned upright and scaled down when large; small audio, video and PDF files as themselves, for a client that can read them. Anything else is described by its type and size, with the post's link. Files over 64 MiB are described without being read. save_file: Save file Saves a file attached to a post into your download directory, set with MM_MCP_DOWNLOAD_DIR and your Downloads directory by default, under its own name, and answers with the path. An existing file is never overwritten: a number is added to the name instead, and saving the same file again answers with the copy already saved. The file is marked as downloaded from the internet, as a browser marks it: on Windows, SmartScreen checks a program and Office opens a document in Protected View; on macOS, Gatekeeper checks it. Files up to 100 MiB. Offered only when mm-mcp runs on your machine, whether writes are allowed or not (below).

docs.title: Post, reply and react
docs.text:
Your MCP client's approval of each call decides, and mm-mcp checks what each states before it acts (below).

create_post: Create post view

Posts a message in a channel, or with root_id replies in the thread of any post in it. Where mm-mcp asks, its question shows the message as it will be sent, the channel and, for a reply, the start of the thread. Posting takes down the typing indicator typing put up there. Returns the post, which an app that shows MCP Apps views shows in the chat as posted, under where it went, as dm and group_message do (Views).

Every call states how far the message goes (below): reaches, how many members the channel has, and notifies where the message alerts a whole channel or user group as Mattermost would ask about first.

files attaches up to ten files: text the model writes, given a name and content, or, when the server runs on your machine over stdio, a file by its full path. Where mm-mcp asks, its question lists each file with its size, type and the path it was read from, the box you tick names every file read from your disk by its path, the files are uploaded only once you accept, and a file changed after you were asked is refused. A file where credentials are kept is never attached (Security); attach such a file in Mattermost yourself if you mean to. dm and group_message take files too.

dm: Send direct message view Sends a direct message to one person, by username or email address, or a note to yourself by your own username. The username is required, so whatever approves the call sees who it goes to. This is how to message people: "message Alice and Bob" is two direct messages. group_message: Send group message view Sends one message to two to seven people together, in the group conversation Mattermost keeps for exactly them. Only when you ask for a group conversation. update_post: Update post Replaces the text of one of your own posts. Where mm-mcp asks, its question shows the current text and its replacement. An edit notifies nobody, so its mentions are not checked, only its length. The call states reaches, how many members the post's channel has, since an edit reaches everyone the post does; old_message, the post's current text in full; and, for a post with reactions or replies, responses, their number (below). Another person's post is refused, even with an administrator's credential. delete_post: Delete post Deletes one of your own posts. Deleting the post that starts a thread deletes its replies, other people's included. The call states deletes, how many posts go: 1 for a reply, or the post and its replies (below). add_reaction: Add reaction Reacts to a post with an emoji, by name, such as thumbsup, or as itself, such as 👍. An unknown name is refused with the closest ones. A reaction joins one others gave under another name of the same emoji, so thumbsup beside a +1 is the one 👍. Reacting again with the same emoji changes nothing. remove_reaction: Remove reaction Takes back one of your reactions. pin_post: Pin post Pins a post to its channel for everyone, or unpins it with pinned false.

docs.title: Channels and people
docs.text: get_me: Who am I The Mattermost user the server acts as: id, username, name, nickname, position, roles, the timezone set in Mattermost, and whether it is a bot. Call it to check the connection and whose access the other tools use. get_users: Get users People by username, user id or email address, any mix of them in one call, with whether each is a bot or deactivated. An email address finds someone only when the server shows you addresses. A name nobody has is listed with the closest usernames beside the people found, and refused only when nobody is found. get_status: Get status Whether people are around: online, away, do not disturb or offline, when they were last active, and the status message they set. get_user_teams: List the user's teams The teams you belong to. get_team_info: Get team A team by id, name or link. An open team you are not in is found by the exact name in its link. get_channel_info: Get channel A channel by id, name or link, among your own channels and the public channels of your teams, saying whether you belong to it and whether it is archived. list_team_channels: List a team's channels A team's public channels, by name. list_archived_channels: List archived channels A team's archived channels. An archived channel can be read but not posted in. get_channel_stats: Get channel stats How many people belong to a channel, how many are guests, and how many posts are pinned and files shared in it. join_channel: Join channel Joins a public channel of one of your teams. Everyone in it sees that you joined. A private channel is joined only by being added. leave_channel: Leave channel Leaves a channel you belong to. Everyone in it sees that you left, and only being added brings you back to a private one, which mm-mcp's question says where it asks. add_channel_members: Add channel members Adds up to twenty people, by username, user id or email address, to a channel you belong to. Each is notified, and where mm-mcp asks, its question names each. create_channel: Create channel Creates a public or private channel in one of your teams, with you in it, the name in its link made from its display name as Mattermost's own app makes it, and its purpose and header when given. set_status: Set status Sets your status as everyone sees it beside your name: online, away, do not disturb until a time, or offline, and a status message with an emoji, until a time or until changed; or clears the message. A time without an offset is read in your timezone.

docs.title: Your own things
docs.text:
propose_post: Propose post view

Proposes a post for you to send yourself. The message waits as your draft, in a channel, a thread, or a direct or group message you already have, in your message box in every Mattermost app, and the answer links where it waits. Nothing is sent. The message is checked as a post's is, and its notes say what its mentions will do. One that starts with / is refused, since Mattermost runs it as a slash command when you send it. Proposing again replaces mm-mcp's own proposal while you have not changed it; a draft you wrote or typed in is never replaced (below). A conversation that does not exist yet is not started, since starting one shows it to the other people at once, and a proposal is refused when your drafts do not sync, since you would never see it. What you send from Mattermost goes out as yours, without the mark of a post written with AI. Whatever your app approves, it is a way to post only what you send yourself.

In an app that shows views, the proposal appears in the chat as it will be posted, where it waits, and what its mentions do, with Post, Edit and Discard (Views). Each acts on the text the view shows, and only while your draft still holds it as the view put it there: a draft you typed on in Mattermost is yours to send from there, and a newer proposal is drawn again as it is now. Post marks the post as written with AI, and asks first where Mattermost would ask: before an @channel or @here reaches more than five people. A link shows where it leads, a character you cannot see or that turns the text's direction is flagged, and the text as written is a click away. Where a draft of yours is in the way, the view shows yours beside the proposal, or the proposal as a revision of yours when your agent says so with revises_draft, and nothing is written until you press Replace mine, or Apply, or Keep mine. MM_MCP_POST_FROM_VIEWS=false takes Post out of the view (Configuration).

list_drafts: List drafts Your drafts, in channels and threads, with where each is, by link and address, and its length, which delete_draft states. delete_draft: Delete draft Deletes your draft in a channel or thread. Nobody else sees a draft, but it may hold words you have not sent, so the call states discards, how many characters the draft holds, as list_drafts gives its length (below), and where mm-mcp asks, its question shows the draft and where it is. set_post_reminder: Set post reminder Has Mattermost remind you of a post at a time, as its "Remind me" does. A time without an offset is read in the timezone you set in Mattermost. save_post: Save post Saves a post among your saved posts, or removes it with saved false. follow_thread: Follow thread Follows a thread, so its replies notify you and it appears in list_threads, or stops following it with following false. mark_channel_read: Mark channel read Marks a channel read, as opening it in Mattermost does, clearing its unread count and mentions, only when you ask for it. Reading a channel for you never marks it read. typing: Show typing Shows you typing in a channel or thread while a message is written, kept up until create_post posts there, stop is sent, or a minute passes. It is optional, for a long message that takes a while to write.

docs.title: Check the setup
docs.text: diagnose: Diagnose mm-mcp The checks mm-mcp doctor makes, from inside the running server, so with the configuration your MCP client actually started it with: the address, which credential it acts with, a login mm-mcp login stored and whether MM_TOKEN hides it, the proxy, whether the server answers as a supported Mattermost, whose credential it is and whether that user belongs to a team. It adds what only the client shows: its name and protocol version, who decides on a write, and, where mm-mcp is set to ask, whether the client can show its question. With ask_test_question, it shows you a test question and reports how it was answered: an answer within a few seconds came from the client itself, which then answers every question before a write without showing it. Each check says what it found, and a failed one what to do. It never returns the credential (Configuration).

docs.title: Works the same everywhere
docs.text:
• Names and links work where ids do, for a tool that reads. Every channel_id and team_id of a tool that reads, or that changes only what is yours, takes a name as well as an id, a channel's with ~ or # before it or not. Every id argument takes the place's address, and the link Mattermost shows you: a channel's, a direct or group message's, a team's, a post's, Copy Link's or the one a thread opens at, and a file's, or its resource address. A name of a channel, a team or a person matches in any case, whole or in part; an ambiguous one is refused with every candidate, and an unknown one with the closest names. A link is never fetched, and one to another server is refused (ADR-030).
  • A write others see takes an address. The tools that post or change what others see take a channel, a post or a team by its address alone, matched exactly: mattermost://<server>/<team>/channels/<channel>, a direct message's mattermost://<server>/<team>/messages/@<username>, a post's as its channel's address followed by its id, and a team's as mattermost://<server>/<team>. Your MCP client's approval of the call, or its AI reviewer, sees the tool's arguments and nothing else, so the address shows where the write goes by name. An id, a name or a link is refused with where to read the address, and so is the old address of a renamed channel.
  • Every place comes with its link and its address. Each post, channel, team and draft an answer describes carries its address, and the link it opens at, and so do the post and channel of each file search_files finds, made from names: a channel's in its team, a direct or group message's in your first team, as /<team>/messages/@<username>, and a post's in its channel's team, as Copy Link gives it. Asked where something was said, the agent links the post, not the conversation. Beside each link is the name Mattermost shows: a channel's display name, and a direct or group message named after the other people in it.
  • Every list pages the same way. Give limit, and pass the next_cursor an answer ends with back as cursor, with the same other arguments, for the next page, until an answer has none (ADR-032).
  • Every post comes back in one shape: its link and address, its author's username and name, its channel by name, link and address and its team by name, its files with their ids and resource addresses, reactions with who reacted, responses, how many reactions and replies it has, whether it is pinned or marked as written with AI, its thread, and when it was edited. An answer whose posts are all in one channel names the channel and team once.
  • A post from a webhook or a bot carries its cards. Integrations such as Alertmanager, Grafana, Jira or a CI server post their content as message attachments, often with no message beside them. Each post gives them as message_attachments, as Mattermost shows them: the pretext, author and its link, title and its link, text, fields, footer and fallback, the color the integration chose for the bar beside them, and the addresses of their pictures, image_url, such as a chart Grafana drew, and thumb_url. Their buttons and menus are left out: pressing one is a change, and it calls the integration. The color is kept where Mattermost draws a bar in it (Supported releases).
  • A post from an integration carries its blocks. From Mattermost 11.11 on, integrations can post their content as blocks, in Mattermost's own format, Slack's Block Kit or Microsoft's Adaptive Cards, often with no message beside them. Where your server shows them, each post gives them as blocks, in one shape whichever format they came in, as Mattermost draws them: text, images by address, dividers, containers with the color of their bar, collapsible sections and columns, as an outline in which a block holds the deeper blocks after it. Mattermost draws a post's blocks in place of its message attachments, and so does mm-mcp. Buttons and menus are left out, as they are of message attachments. A server on an older release does not show blocks, and neither does mm-mcp (Supported releases).
  • A post carries what its first link leads to, as Mattermost shows it below the message. A link to another post gives quoted_post: its author, channel, time, link, message, label and files, so "is this still true?" followed by a link reads whole. Mattermost leaves the quote out for you when you cannot read the post it quotes. A link to a web page gives link_preview with the page's title, description and site, and a link to a picture link_preview with image and its size. As in Mattermost, a post with message attachments shows no preview, and the page's text is its owner's.
  • A post from an integration says so, under the name Mattermost shows. An integration posts under an account, a person's or a bot's, through an incoming webhook or as a slash command's answer. Such a post has from_integration, and a bot's post has author_is_bot: Mattermost tags both BOT. Where your server lets integrations choose their name, shown_as is the name Mattermost shows in place of the account's, and author still names the account. Anyone who can call the integration can choose any name, so the account is the one to trust. show draws such a post as Mattermost does: the name, the BOT tag, and no run with the posts around it.
  • A post marked Important or Urgent says so. Its priority is important or urgent, the label Mattermost shows beside its author's name, and persistent_notifications says Mattermost keeps notifying the people it mentions until they read it. On a licensed server a post can ask everyone to acknowledge it: it has requested_ack, acknowledgements says who did and when, and acknowledged that you did. Each is there only where your server shows it, as Mattermost's settings for message priority and acknowledgements say.
  • A burn-on-read post stays concealed. On a server with an Enterprise Advanced license, someone can send a post of type burn_on_read, which Mattermost conceals from you until you open it there; a while after, it is gone for you. Until you open it, the post has concealed and nothing of what it holds. No tool opens one: your agent can tell you it waits, and its url takes you to it. expire_at is when it is gone for you: once opened, when its timer runs out, and until then, the latest it is kept.
  • A call's post carries the call. The Calls plugin, on by default, starts a call with a post of type custom_calls, and draws its own card in place of the message. Such a post has call: its title, started_at, and once it ended, ended_at and the usernames of its participants. The attachment the plugin adds for clients without the plugin, which repeats the message, is left out. Joining a call is for you to do in Mattermost.
  • A /me post has type me; its message keeps the asterisks Mattermost stores around it and does not show.
  • A reminder from the system bot links to its post with a full URL, even on a server without a site URL, where Mattermost stores only a path.
  • Withheld files are counted. Where an attribute-based access policy (Enterprise Advanced) withholds a post's files from you, withheld_files says how many.
  • A list cuts a long post short. A list shows at most 4,000 characters of a post: its message first, then the text of its message attachments or blocks. What is cut says its whole length, message_length, message_attachments_length or blocks_length; read_post reads it whole.
  • Times are your own. A time in an answer is in the timezone you set in Mattermost, with its offset, such as 2026-10-09T09:30:00+02:00, and a time you give without an offset is read in it too. With no timezone set, UTC.

docs.title: Files as resources
docs.text:
Every file attached to a post is also an MCP resource, at mattermost://<your server>/files/<file id>, from a template mm-mcp lists (ADR-029). A client can read one when it needs it, and some let you attach one to the conversation or save it. It reads as read_file reads the file, but whole: text, a Word, PowerPoint or Excel file's text and an archive's listing as text, an image as the image read_file returns, and anything else as itself, in one message of up to 10 MiB, a binary file counted as its base64: MCP sends a resource whole, and clients drop a larger message. MM_MCP_RESOURCE_MAX_MB changes that for a client that takes more (Configuration). A file larger than your Mattermost now takes in one, its Maximum File Size, is not downloaded. Past a limit, a text is read with read_file, in windows, and a file saved with save_file. Each post's files, and each file search_files finds, give the address, the answer links each file as a resource, and every file_id takes the address. An image also gives its size and its preview's address, at mattermost://<your server>/files/<file id>/preview: the smaller image its post shows, cheaper to look at than the whole image.

The pictures a post shows with it are resources too: a person's profile picture, at mattermost://<your server>/users/<user id>/image, the one they set or the one Mattermost draws from their initials, and a custom emoji's, at mattermost://<your server>/emoji/<name>. Each reads as a picture, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP and never SVG, and one read again within a few minutes comes from what mm-mcp kept rather than from Mattermost. A client that completes resource addresses offers, as you type part of a file's name, the ids of the files that match. Threads and conversations are not resources: a conversation has no end to read it whole to.

docs.title: Views
docs.text: In an AI app that shows MCP Apps views, show puts a thread, or what is unread for you, in the chat as Mattermost lays it out, every post your agent makes shows itself there as posted, and a post it proposes with propose_post waits there for you to post, change or discard (ADR-022). The view is a page in mm-mcp itself, which reaches no network: the app reads what it shows from mm-mcp, and the pictures as resources, with mm-mcp's credential. Where the app reads no pictures, people are their initials and a custom emoji its name, except that a thread shown in Claude Code brings its pictures with it. The page takes the app's light or dark theme and its language, where mm-mcp has words for it, and English otherwise. VS Code shows views with its chat.mcp.apps.enabled setting on, and Claude Code in the Claude desktop app; diagnose says whether yours does. Views shows each of them, live.

docs.text:
What a page holds when limit is not given, and the most it can hold.

Tool Default At most read_channel, read_unread 30 200 read_post 100 200 list_pinned_posts 30 100 search_posts, list_mentions, search_files 20 100 list_saved, list_threads, list_drafts, search_users 20 100 get_user_teams, get_user_channels, search_channels, list_team_channels, list_archived_channels 50 200

docs.title: How a write is checked
docs.text:
Your MCP client's own approval of each call decides whether a change others see goes ahead: its prompt, its permission rules or its auto mode (ADR-033). mm-mcp does not ask you by default. What it controls is what it checks itself, on every call, whoever approved it: how far a post or an edit goes, the text an edit replaces and the reactions and replies that answer it, and what a deletion takes away, each stated in the call and read again just before the write; where it goes, by address; and the message itself. A refusal says what mm-mcp found and tells the model to weigh whether that is what you meant.

A post can also go ahead on your own press. In an app that shows views, a post your agent proposes with propose_post shows with Post, which sends it only while your draft holds what the view shows, after Mattermost's own question where it would ask one (Views). MM_MCP_POST_FROM_VIEWS=false takes Post out of the view.

With MM_MCP_ELICITATION_OPT_IN=true, mm-mcp asks you as well (Configuration): it shows what will change, where, and under whose name, and acts only when you tick the box and accept. The question is an MCP elicitation, a form the client shows, so these tools then need a client that shows one; a client that declares it cannot gets an error that says so, and nothing is written. Some clients declare that they can and decline the form without showing it, as Claude Code does in the Claude desktop app's Code tab. diagnose with ask_test_question tells you whether yours shows it. MM_MCP_FORCE_HUMAN_IN_THE_LOOP_IN_CLAUDE_CODE has Claude Code ask on every call instead.

Every message is checked before the write (ADR-031): one longer than the server takes is refused with its length and the limit, and an @mention of someone nobody is is refused with the closest usernames. Where mm-mcp asks, the question says how many people @here, @channel and @all reach, who of those mentioned is deactivated, and, on a licensed server with user groups, how many a group's mention notifies, and puts what a post does, and every file it carries, before the message. A question about a post quotes what Mattermost shows of it: its message, or for a post with none, such as an alert, the text of its blocks or cards, or else its files' names; never a burn-on-read post you have not opened. An integration's post is named as Mattermost shows it, with the account behind it. Mentions are found as Mattermost finds them, so code mentions nobody and @here. ending a sentence is @here.

docs.title: How far a message goes
docs.text:
create_post states in its call how far the message goes, as two numbers mm-mcp counts itself (ADR-031):

  • reaches, on every post: how many members the channel has. Everyone in it can read the message, whatever it mentions.
  • notifies, exactly where Mattermost's web app would ask before sending, with the number it would show: everyone but you for @channel, @all or @here in a channel of more than 5 members, or a mentioned user group's members in the channel, above 5. As in Mattermost, it is not asked while the server's EnableConfirmNotificationsToChannel is off, or of someone who may not mention the whole channel.

update_post states reaches too, never notifies. The numbers are in the call because that is what your MCP client's own approval shows you, or its AI reviewer, and the model cannot state them without looking. A missing or wrong number is refused with the real one, and the model is told to weigh whether you meant the message for that many people before it calls again. Each is counted again just before the post goes out, so members who joined since the count was read stop it.

For example, when the model posts @channel the release is out in ~Town Square, a channel of 512 members, without stating the numbers, the call is refused with:

Refused

create_post did not run: a message in ~Town Square reaches 512 people, the channel's members as Mattermost counts them, and the call left the number out. Consider whether the person meant this message for all of them. If they did, call again with reaches: 512. If not, send it somewhere narrower, such as a smaller channel or a direct or group message, or ask them where it should go

With reaches: 512 it is refused again, because Mattermost would ask before alerting the whole channel:

Refused

create_post did not run: @channel alerts 511 people, every member of ~Town Square but the user, which Mattermost asks about before sending, and the call left the number out. Consider whether the person meant to alert all of them. If they did, call again with notifies: 511. If not, mention only the people meant, post somewhere narrower, or ask them

The model then calls again with reaches: 512 and notifies: 511, which your client's approval shows you, as does mm-mcp's question where it asks. Nothing is posted until both are right.

docs.title: What an edit changes
docs.text:
update_post states the post's current text in full, old_message, alongside its replacement (ADR-031). The model cannot edit a post without writing out all of what it replaces, and your client's approval shows both texts. An old_message that differs from the post's current text, because you edited the post after the model read it or because only part of it is quoted, is refused with the current text.

A post with reactions, or with replies in the thread it starts, also takes responses, their number, as read_post gives it. An edit leaves those reactions and replies under the replacing text, and Mattermost tells nobody about an edit, so a thumbs up given to one sentence stands under another. For example, an edit of your "Give me a thumbs up if you like cat memes", which has five 👍 and two replies, that leaves out responses is refused with:

Refused

update_post did not run: 7 reactions and replies respond to your post in ~Town Square: :thumbsup: ×5 (@brent, @ann, @joe, 2 more), 2 replies in its thread, and the call left the number out. An edit leaves them under the replacing text, and Mattermost tells nobody about it. Consider whether they fit the replacement; if the change is news to those who responded, reply in the thread instead. If they fit it, call again with responses: 7

A post without reactions or replies takes no responses.

docs.title: What a write takes away
docs.text:
A deletion states how much goes in its call, as a number mm-mcp reads itself: discards, the characters of the draft delete_draft deletes, as list_drafts gives each draft's length; and deletes, the posts delete_post removes, the post and every reply in its thread. A missing or wrong number is refused with the real one and the start of what would go, and the model is told to weigh whether you meant to lose it. Each is counted again just before the write, so a draft you typed on or a reply that arrived since the model read it stops the write.

For example, deleting a post that started a thread of 12 replies, without deletes:

Refused

delete_post did not run: it deletes 13 posts, your post in ~Town Square, which begins “Who is in for the release party on Friday? I'll book a table”, and the 12 replies in its thread, other people's included, and the call left the number out. Consider whether the person meant to delete all of them. If they did, call again with deletes: 13. If not, leave it, or ask the person

A thirteenth reply arriving before the model calls again with deletes: 13 gets the same refusal, with 14.

propose_post takes nothing away. A draft of yours where the proposal would go, one you wrote or typed in, is left as it is. In an app that shows views, the view asks you which to keep; in one that does not, the call is refused with what the draft holds. For example, proposing a reply in ~Town Square, where you started one of your own:

Refused

propose_post did not run: the person has a draft there, which was left as it is: “Sounds good, but can we move it to”. If they asked you to change it, delete it with delete_draft, stating discards: 34, and propose again. If not, they can finish or clear it in Mattermost, or post with create_post

When you asked for your draft to be changed, the model deletes it with delete_draft, whose call states its length, and proposes again.

docs.title: Where a write goes
docs.text:
A write others see names its channel, post or team by its address (above, ADR-030), so your client's approval shows where it goes by name. A post to ~Town Square named by its channel's name, on a server at chat.example.com, is refused with:

Refused

channel_id: ~town-square is a name, but this takes an address, mattermost://chat.example.com/<team>/channels/<channel>, or <team>/messages/@<username> for a direct message, which names the place exactly and shows it to whoever approves the call; get_user_channels, get_channel_info and every post give each channel's address

and a reply whose root_id names the post by its link:

Refused

root_id: https://chat.example.com/eng/pl/4xk3m9p7qfgt8jw1yb5hc2ndre is a link, but this takes an address, mattermost://chat.example.com/<team>/channels/<channel>/<post id>: its channel's address, then its id, which names the place exactly and shows it to whoever approves the call; read_post, read_channel and search_posts give each post's address

The model reads the address, mattermost://chat.example.com/eng/channels/town-square, and calls again with it.

Where mm-mcp asks, what a write acts on is what you were asked about: a reply posted, a file rewritten or a draft typed on while you read the question stops the write. Posts and edits are marked as written with AI, as Mattermost shows it, unless MM_MCP_MARK_AI_GENERATED is false. A proposal is not: what you send from Mattermost is yours.

docs.title: On your machine
docs.text: save_file, and attaching a file by its path, are offered only when mm-mcp runs on your own machine, started by your client over stdio, whether writes are allowed or not: they reach your disk, not Mattermost (ADR-029).

docs.title: Not offered
docs.text:
• Scheduled posts. Mattermost's scheduled posts need a licence, and Team Edition, which mm-mcp is tested against, refuses them (ADR-004).
  • Marking what the model read as read, or anything unread. What you have read is yours to record, and a model reading a channel is not you reading it; mark_channel_read marks a channel read when you ask (ADR-021).

docs.title: How the tools are built
docs.text:
Every tool declares a title and the four MCP annotations: whether it only reads, whether it may destroy something, whether repeating it changes nothing more, and that it works in a closed domain, your one Mattermost server, which the MCP specification counts as closed however freely people write in it (ADR-021). They are hints: a client may use them to decide what to ask you about, or ignore them, and none of them is a security control. Some clients run a tool marked read-only without asking you or their AI reviewer, so only a tool that changes nothing in Mattermost is marked so, and a test holds each one to the endpoints it calls.

Each tool also accounts for every parameter of the Mattermost endpoints it calls: which argument sets it, or why it is fixed or left out (ADR-028), and a live test calls every tool against a real Mattermost (ADR-004).

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
Some AI apps can show more than text: small, interactive panels inside the chat, which MCP calls views. mm-mcp uses views to show you Mattermost as Mattermost shows it. You see a thread you asked about, what you missed, and every post your agent makes. A post your agent drafts for you waits there for you to check, change and send yourself.

Everything below is live. Each view is the same one mm-mcp shows in your AI app, playing back a recorded conversation from a test Mattermost. Press anything: nothing is sent from this page, and Start over puts a view back as it was.

Does my app show views, and what do I need?

VS Code shows them once chat.mcp.apps.enabled is on in its settings. Claude Code shows them in the Claude desktop app, to read. Ask your agent to run diagnose and it tells you whether yours does (Installation).

Seeing a thread, or what you missed, works as soon as mm-mcp is set up. Drafting a post, and Post, Edit, Discard and Mark read in a view, need writes allowed, with MM_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=true (Configuration).

In an app that shows no views, everything still works: your agent answers in words, and a post it drafts waits in Mattermost for you (more below).

docs.title: Check and send a post your agent drafts
docs.text:
Ask your agent to draft something for you, and nothing is posted until you say so. The draft waits in Mattermost's message box, as your own unsent draft, and the view shows it exactly as it will look once posted.

Your agent, with mm-mcp Jordan asks whether the migration is done. Draft a reply for me to check. propose_post, a reply in ~release-planning

Try it: press Edit, change a word, save, then press Post.

  • Post sends it under your name, marked as written with AI, and clears the draft.
  • Edit changes the draft. Once you have changed it, it is yours: your agent will not replace it.
  • Discard deletes the draft.
  • A link shows where it really goes, next to the words it is written as.

If you change the draft in Mattermost while the view is open, the view notices, and leaves the draft to you there instead of sending the old text. If your agent proposes again, your next press shows you the new text first.

docs.title: A message to the whole channel
docs.text:
Mattermost asks before a message with @channel, @all or @here notifies more than five people. The view asks too, with the number of people it will notify, counted as Mattermost counts them.

Try it: press Post, then Cancel or Post anyway.

docs.title: When you already started a message there
docs.text:
Mattermost keeps one unsent draft in each channel and in each thread. If yours is already there, your agent never writes over it:

  • You asked your agent to improve it: the view shows the suggested changes, word by word, with Apply and Keep mine.
  • Otherwise: the view shows your draft next to the suggestion, with Replace mine and Keep mine.

Nothing is changed until you press.

docs.title: See a thread
docs.text:
Ask to see a thread and your agent shows it with show. You get pictures, formatting, reactions, custom emoji, images that open full size in their post, and the cards a webhook or bot posts, such as an alert with its red or green bar, and the blocks an integration posts on Mattermost 11.11 and later, with their columns and the sections you unfold. A link to another post shows that post quoted below it, a long one cut short with Show more for the rest: press the quote to read the post, in the view where your app allows it and otherwise in Mattermost. A link to a web page shows the page's card. A picture a link or a card leads to is named, and opens in your browser: the view itself reaches nothing outside Mattermost. A post marked Important or Urgent carries its label, and one that asks to be acknowledged says how many did, with who when you point at it. A burn-on-read message you have not opened stays concealed, as in Mattermost: View message in Mattermost takes you there to open it. A call shows when it started and by whom, or when it ended, how long it lasted and who was in it. A long thread loads more as you ask.

Try it: press 2 more replies, or the chart to see it full size.

docs.title: See what you missed
docs.text:
Ask what you missed, and the view lists:

  • your channels with unread messages, by team;
  • the posts that mention you;
  • the threads you follow that have new replies.

Open a channel right there to read it. Where your agent may post, Mark read marks it read in Mattermost too.

Try it: press Design to open it, then Mark read.

docs.title: See what your agent posted
docs.text: When your agent posts for you with create_post, dm or group_message, the post shows in the chat as it was posted, and where. An agent that posts in many places cannot do so out of your sight.

docs.title: If your app shows no views
docs.text:
Every app still works. A post your agent drafts waits in Mattermost's message box in every Mattermost app you use, and your agent's answer links to the place where it waits. Send it, change it or clear it there.

docs.title: Which apps show views
docs.text:
App Views Good to know VS Code Yes, with chat.mcp.apps.enabled on VS Code asks you before your agent drafts a post, as it does before anything that writes. Your own press in a view is not asked about again. Claude Code, in the Claude desktop app Yes, to read Threads and what you missed show, and on an https server a link opens after a confirmation. The button beside a view opens it in a pane of its own, where an open image fills the pane. As of Claude Code 2.1.309 it passes nothing from a view on to mm-mcp, so a thread brings its pictures along, up to 1 MiB, and only an image's preview opens large. In the other views people show as initials, and a draft waits in Mattermost for you to send, with no Post, Edit or Discard. In a terminal, Claude Code shows text. Codex Not checked Nobody has tried it yet. In an app that shows no views, everything still works in words. Goose, the desktop app Yes In its "approve" and "smart approve" modes, Goose blocks every button in a view. The view then says so and offers to open Mattermost instead. Claude desktop, Claude on the web Not confirmed These apps cannot be tested by machine. A check by hand is recorded on mm-mcp#37. An app without views No Your agent answers in words, and drafts wait in Mattermost.

VS Code and Goose are tested with every change to mm-mcp, because a machine can drive them.

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Can my agent press Post for me? No. The buttons in a view go through a tool that only the view can use: your AI app keeps it away from the agent. Your app is trusted to do that, and to press only when you click. mm-mcp cannot tell a click from a script, so where that trust is not there, an administrator can take Post out of the view with MM_MCP_POST_FROM_VIEWS=false (Configuration). The draft then waits in Mattermost for you to send. Will people see that AI wrote my post? A post you send with Post in the view is marked as written with AI, as every post mm-mcp makes is; Mattermost shows that next to it. A draft you send from Mattermost yourself is not marked: it is yours. An administrator can turn the mark off with MM_MCP_MARK_AI_GENERATED=false. Can it send something different from what I see? No. Post sends the text the view shows, and only while your draft still holds exactly that, as the view put it there. If you typed in the draft, or attached a file to it, in Mattermost, the view leaves it to you to send from there; if your agent proposed again, the view shows you the new text instead of sending. The preview hides nothing: a link shows where it leads, a link definition Mattermost does not show is shown, and a character you cannot see, or one that turns the text's direction, is flagged, even when it is written as its number. Here, the name invoice_fdp.exe is made to read as invoice_exe.pdf: Does my agent know what I did? Your app may pass it on: the view tells it, in a fixed sentence, whether you posted, changed or discarded the draft. Not every app passes that on, so your agent can also check Mattermost: the draft gone, or the post in the channel. Does the view send my data anywhere? No. The view reaches no network. What it shows comes from mm-mcp through your app, pictures included, and mm-mcp talks to nothing but your Mattermost (Security). For the technically curious: what happens when you press Post 
sequenceDiagram
    actor You
    participant App as Your AI app
    participant Model as The AI model
    participant mm as mm-mcp
    participant MM as Mattermost
    Model->>mm: propose_post, the message
    mm->>MM: save it as your draft, marked as mm-mcp's proposal
    mm-->>App: the draft
    App->>You: the view: the post as it will be posted
    You->>App: Post
    App->>mm: view_change, post, the text the view shows
    mm->>MM: does the draft still hold that text, and nothing else?
    mm->>MM: post it, marked as written with AI, and delete the draft
    mm-->>App: posted

Technically, a view is an MCP Apps view: a page that ships inside mm-mcp, which your app runs in a sandbox without network access. Its buttons call view_change, a tool marked for views alone, which mm-mcp offers only to an app that says it shows views, and only once writes are allowed. The decisions behind this are in ADR-022 and ADR-035.

docs.title: ADR-001: Go, the official MCP SDK, and Mattermost's own client
docs.text:
mm-mcp is written in Go, at the toolchain go.mod pins, and serves MCP through the official Go SDK, github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk. It reaches Mattermost through Mattermost's own Go client and types, model.Client4 and the model package from the server's public module (ADR-024). It ships as one static binary per platform (ADR-023).

The decisive reason is the data layer. Client4 and the model structs are the server's own code: the structs are what the server serialises, and Mattermost's API test suite drives the server through Client4 on every commit. Mattermost's published OpenAPI specification is written by hand and tested by nothing, and is wrong in ways only a live call reveals: its User schema has no is_bot field, which the struct cannot lack. The server's source at each release tag is also the most exact record of what changed between releases. The public module is Apache-2.0, as this project is.

Write handlers with typed input and output structs, so the SDK derives and validates both schemas. Use the model types for what mm-mcp sends to and reads from Mattermost, and a struct of mm-mcp's own for what a tool returns, holding only what the model needs. Do not add a second MCP library or a second Mattermost client.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• Python on FastMCP, with a client generated from the OpenAPI specification: Built and measured first. The specification needed seven repairs before a generator would accept it and still lacked fields the server sends, and every repair was a belief to keep current. FastMCP's ready-made HTTP authentication would have been the real loss had mm-mcp been hosted, which it is not (ADR-020).
  • TypeScript: Mattermost's web client is TypeScript, but the server's own Go types and client are what its API tests exercise.

docs.title: ADR-002: Every workflow is a task, and every tool's version is pinned in one place
docs.text:
Every workflow in this repository is a task in Taskfile.yml, run as task <name>, and CI runs the same tasks a developer does rather than copies of their steps. The Go toolchain is pinned by the toolchain directive in go.mod, and Go fetches it when the installed one is older. Tools that are not Go module dependencies are pinned in .github/tool-versions.env, which the Taskfile loads and CI reads: golangci-lint, govulncheck, GoReleaser, Task itself, the MCP Registry's publisher, Komac, the mcpb tool and the Node that runs it among them. CI installs a tool that publishes binaries from its release, held to the release's checksums, rather than building it: .github/actions/setup-task puts Task on the PATH in seconds, where go install took a minute a job. TestEveryToolVersionIsPinnedInOnePlace refuses a version a workflow or the Taskfile states itself (ADR-015). The documentation site's Python tooling is a uv project in docs/, locked by docs/uv.lock. A contributor installs Go, Task, Docker and git; lefthook and uv are recommended.

Add a workflow as a task and have CI call the task. Pin a new tool in .github/tool-versions.env, never in a workflow alone. Write logic a task needs in Go under tools/, one directory per command, when it has a purpose no existing tool serves; the reason for each is in its package comment. Keep a task's commands to what Task's built-in shell runs on every platform; a task that needs bash says so in its description.

A version stated in two places can disagree, and the disagreement shows as a check that passes locally and fails in CI. Task is cross-platform and declarative, and Go tools under tools/ run anywhere the module builds.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• Make: Not installed on Windows by default, and its recipes run in whichever shell the platform has.
  • Shell scripts for the tooling: They do not run the same on Windows; tools/ in Go does.

docs.title: ADR-003: AI agents as first-class developers
docs.text:
Agents are first-class contributors here, and everything a contributor needs to know is written down where an agent finds it: AGENTS.md for the mechanics and pitfalls of working in this repository, CONTRIBUTING.md for the process, the decision records for the rules and why they hold, the docs for how mm-mcp behaves, and a focused comment beside code whose reason the code does not show. Nothing depends on tribal knowledge or on a convention inferred from the code. When you find a recurring convention that is written nowhere, propose a record or an AGENTS.md entry for it. AGENTS.md repeats the rules from CONTRIBUTING.md that an agent must not lose, because an agent keeps AGENTS.md in context through compaction and drops a file it read once; change such a rule in both.

A decision record states a rule as it holds now, in prose: the rule first, then why it holds, with what a contributor or an agent must do in the same prose, and the alternatives turned down under Not chosen. CONTRIBUTING.md, under Writing a decision record, has the shape. Keep it short: an agent carries what it reads in its context, where a sentence with no rule, reason or instruction in it is noise. An agent reads a record as authoritative and cannot tell a stale one from a live one, so a record that stops holding is changed or deleted, never left standing.

An agent needs the same context a person does, and a session keeps none of it. Standards written down explicitly keep the next session, and the next contributor, consistent with the last.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• Conventions in code comments alone: Comments are scattered, and rarely capture a rule that spans the repository.
  • Let agents infer conventions from the code: Slower, inconsistent, and it copies whatever the code got wrong.

docs.title: ADR-004: Live tests against a real Mattermost are the correctness gate
docs.text:
Behaviour that depends on Mattermost is proven against a real Mattermost, in the live suite under tests/live, which carries the live build tag. What the server does is authoritative. Client4 and the model types say what a request sends and an answer holds (ADR-024), and the OpenAPI specification says what an endpoint accepts (ADR-026); neither says what the server does with it. Every MCP tool is called by at least one live test that asserts on what it returned, and TestEveryToolIsCalledByALiveTest fails when one is not. A tool counts as called only through an mcp.CallToolParams{Name: "..."} literal the scan can read, so keep the tool's name in the literal.

A live test that writes reads the result back with a separate request, as another user where that is what the tool claims, and writes a value other than the default. A 2xx proves nothing: Mattermost accepts a field it does not know and answers success, and a default reads back the same whether or not the write landed.

When a change does anything beyond parsing or local validation, add or update a live test. To fix a bug, reproduce it with a live test first, then look for the same assumption elsewhere and reproduce that too, then fix it, then break each new test by reverting the fix and watch it fail.

A test built from what its author believes about the API agrees with the code whenever that belief is the bug; only the server can disagree. Permissions, channel membership and server configuration behave in ways no description of the API captures.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• Contract tests or recorded fixtures: They encode what the server was believed or seen to do, and keep passing when it does something else.
  • Trust Client4 because Mattermost tests it: Mattermost tests that its client and server agree, not that a tool asks for what its user meant, nor how an older release answers.

docs.title: ADR-005: Unit tests do not simulate Mattermost
docs.text:
A unit test does not stand a fake Mattermost in front of the code under test. Anything whose outcome depends on how the server behaves, such as which route it serves, what it accepts, what it returns, which status it answers with and what an omitted field means, is proven in the live suite (ADR-004) or it is not proven. Unit tests keep what needs no server: configuration and argument parsing, validation, formatting, logic over data held in memory, the reading of an error already in hand, the annotations and schemas a tool declares, and assertions that the code refuses input before any request is made.

A stand-in stays only where it claims nothing about Mattermost: a round tripper whose subject is the request itself, such as which host it went to; a fault below the API, such as a refused connection; or one that fails the test when it is called, proving no request was made. An httptest.Server that answers a Mattermost route with a Mattermost-shaped body, or a fake of internal/mattermost that returns Mattermost data, is what this record rules out.

When a fix needs a test, write it live first, and reach for a unit test only when no request is involved. If an existing stand-in has to be edited to let a correct change land, it was asserting a wrong belief: delete it and cover the behaviour live.

A mock encodes its author's belief about the API, so when that belief is the defect the mock agrees with the code and the test passes. A mock correct today and wrong after a Mattermost upgrade fails no differently from a right one; only a real server tells them apart.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• Keep mocks, held to a stricter standard: It asks a reviewer to spot an assumption that looks correct by construction, and leaves the drift between releases untouched.
  • Mock through Client4's own types: Real types make a fake look authoritative; the answer it gives is still its author's belief.

docs.title: ADR-006: A unit test inherits nothing and reaches nothing beyond the machine
docs.text:
Every package under cmd/ and internal/ that has tests seals its process in TestMain with testsupport.SealedMain, which empties every variable mm-mcp reads, listed in config.EnvironmentVariables, and sets MM_MCP_BLOCK_EXTERNAL_NETWORK to 1. While that is set, network.NewSafeTransport, the transport every HTTP client in mm-mcp is built on, refuses any host but localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1, and the error names the host it refused. TestEveryTestPackageIsSealed fails a package that has tests and no seal, and TestEveryVariableTheSourceNamesIsListed fails when the code names a variable the list, and so the seal, leaves out.

Build every HTTP client on network.NewSafeTransport. Read configuration through a function that takes a Getenv, as config.FromEnv and cli.Run do, and have a test pass the values it wants with testsupport.Env rather than publish them to the process; t.Setenv is for a test whose subject is the environment, and rules out t.Parallel. Add a variable mm-mcp reads to config.EnvironmentVariables and to the configuration page in the same change.

Unsealed, the machine decides what a test sees: a developer with MM_URL and MM_TOKEN in their shell runs different inputs than a clean runner, and a green run on one is no evidence about the other. An unintended network call makes a suite slow and flaky, fails on an isolated runner, and lets code under test act on a real server with a real token.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• Clear the environment test by test: Every test has to remember to, the one that forgets reads the developer's token, and t.Setenv makes a test sequential.
  • Block the network with a mocking library: It covers the clients it is told about, not one added later.

docs.title: ADR-007: Each checkout runs its own Mattermost Team Edition instances in Docker
docs.text:
The live suite runs against Mattermost Team Edition with PostgreSQL, started by Docker Compose from docker/latest for the newest release and docker/esr for the Extended Support Release (ADR-025). task stack:up starts one, STACK=esr choosing the other and RELEASE=<x.y.z> any other release from the latest stack's file, and tools/stack waits for it to answer and creates its system administrator. task test:live starts the instance before it runs, so a fresh clone needs only Docker.

Every checkout has its own instances, so worktrees never share one and one worktree's restart or reset never ends another's run. The main checkout's projects are mm-mcp-latest on port 8065 and mm-mcp-esr on 8066. A linked worktree's are named after it and a hash of its path, on ports Docker assigns; so is any release run beside them. Docker assigns a new port each time a stopped container starts, so task stack:up writes the instance's address to .tmp/stack-.env every time, and the live suite reads it from there; MM_LIVE_URL points it anywhere else. Containers and volumes carry the label dev.mm-mcp.worktree with the path of the checkout that started them. task stack:up first takes down other checkouts' stopped instances, which frees their networks, and removes the data of any whose worktree no longer exists; it never touches a running one, and refuses to start more than MM_STACK_MAX instances on one machine.

Team Edition is free and needs no licence, and this project pays for none, so every pull request, a fork's included, runs the live suite. A feature only the licensed editions have, such as guest accounts or LDAP groups, is not supported until it can be tested. The instance is configured through docker/mattermost.env, never by a test changing a server setting another test could observe. The administrator's credentials are well known on purpose, and the instance listens on the loopback address only.

Start and stop instances through the tasks, not with docker compose by hand, so names, ports, labels and the state file stay in step. When a test needs server configuration the stack does not have, change docker/mattermost.env for every test, and say why in the commit.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• One shared instance for every checkout: A restart in one worktree ends another's live run, and a fixture one run removes is one another run is using.
  • A trial licence for Enterprise features: It expires, it is a secret forks cannot have, and it buys features the people this serves mostly do not have.
  • The mattermost-preview image: Simpler, but not what anyone deploys, and its tags do not track the Extended Support Release.

docs.title: ADR-008: A live test seeds and owns its fixtures, and names them at random
docs.text:
Every live test seeds the state it needs and owns it. The helpers in tests/live/harness_test.go, such as seedUser and seedBot, create a user, a bot, and in time a team and channels of the test's own through an administrator's Client4, and register their removal with t.Cleanup: a user is deactivated and a bot disabled, because permanent deletion is off by default. No test reads another's fixtures or depends on the order tests run in, so every live test calls t.Parallel and the suite runs as many at once as LIVE_PARALLEL in Taskfile.yml says. A test that asserts on what the whole instance shares, such as a search, looks for its own fixtures by their unique names or content.

A fixture's name is the prefix lt-, the kind of fixture, and a random part from uniqueName, which draws from crypto/rand: never a timestamp, a timestamp with a counter beside it, or a timestamp cut short. The prefix traces a fixture left behind to the suite, and task stack:reset deletes the instance's data when leftovers build up.

When a test needs a new kind of state, add a helper that creates it and registers its removal. Do not seed shared state once for the suite. Mattermost indexes search asynchronously, so a test that searches for what it just posted waits with a bounded poll that fails with what it saw, never with a fixed sleep.

Shared state makes a failure depend on what ran before it, which is the expensive kind to debug, and it stops tests running at the same time. Clock-derived names collide: the clock is coarser than the suite is parallel, and a counter restarts with the process, so a run collides with what a crashed run left behind.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• Clean the instance before every run: It depends on a teardown that a crash is what prevents, and does nothing about two tests colliding inside one run.
  • One seeded team and channel set for the whole suite: Every test that writes changes what the others read.

docs.title: ADR-009: Tests are sorted by what they need, and none of them skips
docs.text:
A unit test needs nothing beyond the machine it runs on. task test:unit runs every package under cmd/, internal/ and tools/; the pre-commit hook runs that task, and CI runs it on Linux, Windows and macOS, and under the race detector on Linux. A test that needs more carries a build tag and has a task of its own: live for a real Mattermost, in tests/live (task test:live); browser for the browsers on the machine, in internal/login (task test:browser), which CI runs on Linux, Windows and macOS with each runner's Chrome, Edge and Firefox and Playwright's Chromium, so mm-mcp login is proven where it ships (ADR-019); views for the view page in Chromium, inside the official MCP Apps bridge, in internal/views (task test:views), which CI runs on Linux with Playwright's Chromium (ADR-022); and clients, with live, for the views in real clients, Goose and VS Code, against a real Mattermost, in tests/live (task test:clients), which CI runs on Linux under Xvfb (ADR-036). Without a tag, go test ./... needs no Mattermost and no browser. task test:live:compile builds the live suite without running it, so a change that breaks it fails in seconds rather than in the live job.

Tests run on every operating system. A test decides by the capability it needs and asserts on every system rather than skipping one by name. A test that cannot reach its dependency fails and says what is missing: the live suite exits before running anything when no Mattermost answers, naming the address it tried and the task that starts one.

Put a test that needs an outside dependency behind a tag and a task, so the fast suite stays fast and needs no setup. Do not call t.Skip on a missing dependency, and do not write a test that runs on one operating system only unless the code it tests is built for that system alone.

A skipped test reads as a passing one: a run that skipped everything reports success having proven nothing, and a skip on one system is coverage that never ran there. mm-mcp ships for all three systems.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• Skip when a dependency is missing: The run stays green on a machine that cannot run the test, so nobody learns that it did not.
  • Live and unit tests in one suite: Every commit would wait for a Mattermost, and a contributor without Docker could not run the tests at all.

docs.title: ADR-010: Conventional Commits, and git hooks run by lefthook
docs.text:
Every commit subject is a Conventional Commit, type(scope): description, with ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer marking a breaking change. The type decides whether a commit reaching main cuts a release, and how large (ADR-013), and the release notes are built from the subjects, so a wrong type ships a wrong version. No hook checks a subject; a reviewer does.

lefthook runs the git hooks configured in lefthook.yml: the unit tests before a commit, and before a push task quality:verify and the docs build. They are recommended rather than required, because CI runs the same gates on every pull request and CI is what refuses a change; a hook only tells you sooner. Install them with lefthook install. Do not skip a hook. A new gate that needs no Mattermost goes into task quality:verify, which the pre-push hook runs and CI runs step by step; govulncheck alone runs in CI only (ADR-014).

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text:
• pre-commit, the Python framework: A Python toolchain to install for a Go project, with versions pinned in its own configuration.
  • A commit-msg hook that validates subjects: It runs only where it is installed, so it cannot be relied on, and a reviewer reads the subject anyway.

docs.title: ADR-011: Every change integrates on next, linearly, and only main releases
docs.text:
next is a permanent branch, and every change integrates there through a pull request merged by rebase: features, fixes and Dependabot's updates alike. The repository allows no merge commit and no squash, and the ruleset on next and main requires a pull request, a passing CI Complete and linear history, and refuses a force push. main moves only when next is promoted onto it, and only main releases (ADR-013). CI runs in full on both branches, live suite included, and its Release Flow job refuses every pull request into main.

A promotion is a fast-forward push of next to main, git push origin origin/next:main, made by an administrator after task release:promote:check confirms that main is an ancestor of next and that CI Complete passed on next's tip. The push bypasses the ruleset's pull request requirement, so the release workflow refuses to release a commit on which CI Complete has not succeeded. main takes no commit that next lacks, so the push is always a fast-forward and neither branch is rewritten.

Branch from next and open every pull request against it; retarget one opened against main. Bring a branch up to date by rebasing it onto next (task pr:rebase), never by merging next into it. A pull request branch is yours to rewrite as often as it helps, by amending, rebasing and force-pushing with lease; next and main are never rewritten. Do not add a release trigger to next or tag from it. When adding a branch to CI's triggers, add it to both the pull request and the push list.
